data.name: CompatibilityWarningText
data.value:
Here you can find advanced compatibility options. These options can solve compatibility problems or make the game faster as well as make the game unstable or not functional.
Empire Earth is an old game and although it requires very little performance, it will run poorly on many computers, especially laptops.
However you should be able to solve many problems with these options, but finding the right combination of settings can take some time.

data.name: RepairStepDownloadPackage
data.value: Close the game. Download the package "Empire Earth Community" again from its release page below, unpack the ZIP file and run "Empire Earth Community Setup" from the unpacked folder: it repairs or updates the games it installed. Do not use the setup from empireearth.eu for this: it is a different setup and would undo the fixes of the package.

The first quoted text is the name of the package, the second the name of the suite setup file; the release page is the GitHub page of the package shown below the steps. empireearth.eu is not translated.

data.name: RepairStepUpdateWithNewPackage
data.value: The update server of empireearth.eu reports this version for its own setups. Your installation comes from the package "Empire Earth Community", which brings its own setups and gets newer versions only as a new release: look on its release page below whether there is a newer one. If there is, close the game, unpack the new package and run "Empire Earth Community Setup" from it. A setup from empireearth.eu would undo the fixes of the package.
data.comment: The only setup step of the advice of an available update when the suite installed the product (since launcher 1.1.1): the version above comes from the update server, which knows the setups of empireearth.eu, not the package; running the suite of the unpacked folder again would install the same versions. The first quoted text is the name of the package, the second the name of the suite setup file; the release page is the GitHub page of the package shown below the steps. empireearth.eu is not translated.

data.name: CleanupInfo
data.value: Leftovers of removed installations (SSSI, Mad Doc, NeoEE) can disturb a new installation. The launcher deletes only entries of your Windows account, only when no installation uses them and their game folder is gone, and only after it has exported them to the backup folder. Entries for all users are only shown, with advice. Software\Sierra is never deleted: it contains the NeoEE CD keys.
data.comment: Below the heading of the registry cleanup (R5, ADR 0007).

data.name: CleanupNothingToCleanUp
data.value: Nothing to clean up: no entry of your account is a leftover.
data.comment: Registry cleanup without a key the launcher could delete (ADR 0007 plan review); the read-only list follows.

data.name: CleanupCandidatesFormat
data.value: {0} entries of your account are leftovers of a removed installation. Select the ones to delete.
data.comment: Registry cleanup with keys the launcher can delete. {0}: their number.

data.comment: Button of the registry cleanup; at most about 26 characters.

data.name: CleanupConfirmFormat
data.comment: Confirmation of the registry cleanup. {0}: the keys, one per line; {1}: the backup folder.

data.name: CleanupOfferedFormat

data.comment: Read-only advice for a stale HKLM key (SSSI or Mad Doc only, ADR 0007 plan review). {0}: the key; {1}: its folder.

data.value: {0}: do not delete, it contains the NeoEE CD keys ({1}).
data.comment: Read-only entry of Software\Sierra (contract 3.8). {0}: the key; {1}: CleanupCdKeysExist, CleanupCdKeysMissing or CleanupCdKeysUnknown.

data.name: ToolsNetworkHeading
data.comment: Heading of the network diagnostics on the Tools page.

data.name: NetworkInfo
data.value: On request the launcher checks what the support forum asked again and again: the network adapters of this computer, the name lookup (DNS) of the NeoEE servers, the update server, the NeoEE status server, NeoEE.cfg and WONLobby.cfg of the game folders (only read) and upnp_info.txt. It sends nothing but the AppId of the installation and the question for the latest game version to the update server and asks no service for your public address.
data.comment: Below the heading of the network diagnostics (R7, ARCHITECTURE 4.6). Keep the file names untranslated.

data.name: NetworkCheckButton
data.comment: Button of the network diagnostics; at most about 26 characters.

data.name: NetworkChecking
data.comment: State line while the network diagnostics run (up to about 20 seconds).

data.name: NetworkVerdictServerAnswersFormat
data.value: The NeoEE server answers ({0} players online). If the lobby still fails, see the hints below and the WON login on this page.
data.comment: Outage verdict: the status server answered. {0}: the number of online players.

data.name: NetworkVerdictOutage
data.value: Probably a server outage, not your computer: the server names resolve and the update server answers, but the NeoEE server does not. Try again later; nothing needs to be changed on this computer.
data.comment: Outage verdict (forum report section 8 row 9, not droppable): DNS works, the update API answers, the status server does not.

data.name: NetworkVerdictNameNotResolvedFormat
data.value: The update server answers, but the name {0} of the NeoEE server cannot be resolved. The DNS server of your connection may have a problem, or the server name has changed: try again later or restart the router.
data.comment: Outage verdict: the update API answers, DNS of the status server fails. {0}: the host name.

data.name: NetworkVerdictNoConnection
data.value: This computer seems to have no internet connection: the name of the NeoEE server cannot be resolved and the update server does not answer. Check the network connection (cable, Wi-Fi, flight mode).
data.comment: Outage verdict: DNS fails and the update API does not answer (or could not be asked).

data.name: NetworkVerdictNoServerReached
data.value: No server answers although the names resolve. A firewall, an antivirus program or a proxy may block the launcher, or both servers are down. Check the exceptions of the firewall and the antivirus program, then try again.
data.comment: Outage verdict: DNS works, but neither the update API nor the status server answers.

data.name: NetworkVerdictUndetermined
data.value: The NeoEE server does not answer. Whether the server is down cannot be told: the update server is only asked with the AppId of an installation of the community setup, and there is none.
data.comment: Outage verdict: DNS works, the status server does not answer, the update API was not asked (no AppId, ADR 0008).

data.name: NetworkVerdictNotConfigured
data.value: The NeoEE server is not configured (the server settings in Empire Earth Launcher.exe.config are invalid), so it was not asked.
data.comment: Outage verdict: no status server settings. Keep the file name untranslated.

data.name: NetworkHintNoConnection
data.value: No connected network adapter has an IPv4 gateway: the computer seems to be offline.
data.comment: Hint of the network diagnostics.

data.name: NetworkHintIPv6Only
data.value: Your connection has IPv6 but no IPv4 gateway. Empire Earth needs IPv4: ask your provider for an IPv4 connection.
data.comment: Hint of the network diagnostics (IPv6 only, forum t=11057 p=48100).

data.name: NetworkHintVirtualAdaptersFormat
data.value: {0} virtual or VPN adapters are connected (for example Hamachi, a VPN or a virtual machine). In the lobby options and in the game's multiplayer options choose the same real adapter with the IPv4 address of your home network; a virtual adapter can hide hosted games or crash the game.
data.comment: Hint of the network diagnostics (forum 4.10). {0}: their number.

data.name: NetworkHintSeveralAdaptersFormat
data.value: {0} network adapters are connected with a gateway (for example cable and Wi-Fi). Choose the same one in the lobby options and in the game's multiplayer options.
data.comment: Hint of the network diagnostics (forum 4.10). {0}: their number.

data.name: NetworkHintCgnat
data.value: The router reports an address of carrier-grade NAT (100.64.0.0/10): your provider shares one public address with other customers, so port forwarding cannot work. NeoEE's RIP hosting still works for normal games; for scenarios and saved games ask your provider for a public IPv4 address.
data.comment: Hint of the network diagnostics (upnp_info.txt, CGNAT, forum 4.9).

data.name: NetworkHintDsLite
data.value: The router has no public IPv4 address of its own and the computer uses IPv6: probably DS-Lite. Port forwarding for IPv4 cannot work; NeoEE's RIP hosting still works for normal games. For scenarios and saved games ask your provider for a public IPv4 address (in the forum this solved it).
data.comment: Hint of the network diagnostics (upnp_info.txt and IPv6, DS-Lite, t=11057 p=48100).

data.name: NetworkHintNoExternalIPv4
data.value: The router reports no external IPv4 address (0.0.0.0). Port forwarding needs one; check the internet connection of the router.
data.comment: Hint of the network diagnostics (upnp_info.txt).

data.name: NetworkHintPrivateExternal
data.value: The router's external address is a private one: a second router or modem is in front of it (double NAT). Forward the ports on both devices, or switch the modem to router or bridge mode.
data.comment: Hint of the network diagnostics (upnp_info.txt, double NAT, forum 4.9).

data.name: GraphicsWindowSizeInfo
data.value: Choose the size of the game window. The launcher saves it in the settings of your Windows account (Game Window Width and Game Window Height) after a backup; nothing else changes. Sizes up to 1920x1200 are offered (1920x1200 only on a screen that is at least that tall), because the game can crash at larger sizes. The menus of the game are made for 4:3 (1024x768); with a widescreen size the picture can be cut off there. A repair or update with the setup writes the recommended size again, then choose it again. The game also has its own resolution option; the one saved last counts.
data.comment: Explanation under the heading of the Graphics page. 1920x1200 is the limit of contract 3.3 (revision 6); the registry value names are not translated.

data.name: ModsInfo
data.value: dreXmod 3 comes with presets: folders in Data\dxm\mods with sounds, textures, fonts and a lobby theme. The file dreXmod.config chooses one of them as the active mod (block Mod: the sounds and textures of the game) and one as the active lobby theme (block LobbyTheme: the look of the lobby), independently of each other. This page only shows the presets and the choice; the launcher changes nothing.
data.comment: Explanation at the top of the Mods page (launcher 1.1.0, read-only).

data.name: ModsHowTo
data.value: To switch by hand: click "Open dreXmod.config" for the game, set Enabled to 1 and Name to the name of a folder (the name at the beginning of each entry above) in the block Mod or LobbyTheme, save the file and start the game. What dreXmod does with a name that is no folder has not been verified.
data.comment: How to switch the preset by hand (the launcher does not). The quoted words are the caption of ModsOpenConfigButton.

data.name: ModsNote
data.value: A setup run (installation, update or repair) installs dreXmod.config anew, so the choice goes back to the shipped default (mod off, lobby theme dxm). Presets you made yourself in Data\dxm\mods stay; the setup does not delete them. Whether an active mod has an effect in multiplayer or ranked games has not been verified: use one there only if you know it is accepted.
data.comment: Note at the bottom of the Mods page: the setup resets the choice but keeps self-made presets; the multiplayer effect is unverified.
